entries.source: Geschichte der Grafen von Wertheim von den ältesten bis zu ihrem Erlöschen im Mannsstamme im Jahre 1556, Nr. XXXIX. , S. 64, XXXIX.
entries.german: xxxx. Graf Rudolf von Wertheim gibt seine Einwilligung, dass Petrissa, die Wittwe des Ritters Craflo von Reicholsheira, ihre Güter daselbst an das Kloster Brombach verkauft. 1286. In nomine Domini amen. Nos Rudolfus Comes de Wert heim tenore presentium notitie universorum, ad quos liiere presentes pervenerint, duximus declarandum, quod Petrissa relicta Craftonis de Reicholsheim et Agnes filia sua omnia sua bona, que in domibus, pascuis, pratis, aquis, silvis et agris eultis et incultis et censibus vel aliis reditibus quibus- eunque jure hereditarie proprietatis in Reicholsheim possi- debant vel de manu nostra titulo feudi obtinebant, vendide- runt fratribus monasterii de Brunnebach pro quinquaginta libris hall. quos ab ipsis in prompta peeunia pereeperunt et in usus suos converterunt, in meram proprietatem perpetuo jure possidenda, accedente super eundem contractum consensu Heroldi filii Ottonis de Heigenstat, generi dicte Petrisse cum nostro assensu pariter et favore. Unde eadem Petrissa et Agnes fdia sua quocunque e bonis predictis titulo feudi de manu nostra videbantur habere, nobis per manus Conra- di de Clinghart pure et libere resignarunt prefato Heroldo, Petrisse genero cum omnibus heredibus eorum tam huic facto quam prelibato tenori consensum plenum in onmibus adhibentes. Nos vero attendentes benevolentiam et devotionem prefatorum fratrum de Brunnebach hactenus erga nos habi- tiun, omnia bona predieta, que ad nos rationc et titulo feudi conferendi speetabant, libere et absolute conferimus et donamus fratribus supradictis in veram et liberam pro- prietatem spe et intuitu eternorum, ut perpetua Iibertate et jure legitime et mere proprietatis possideant, contradictione qualiumeunque non obstante. In cujus rei testimonium et evidens argumentum ne in posterum super premissis ulla possit ambiguitatis et calumniandi occasio suboriri, litcram hanc inde conscriptam nostro sigillo et venerabilis Abbatis de Brunaebach, in cujus presentia hec omuia sunt pertrac- 45 tata, duximus municndam. Testes sunt: Godfridus nobilis de Slüsselberc. Conradus Clinckart. Wolframus de Kuntech. God fridus de Arrstein. Otto filius Lupoldi. Cnappo scultetus de Wertheim. Hermannus Cellarius ibidem. Godfridus frater ejus- dem. Fridericus Nusekel et alii quam plures. Actum et da- tum anno incarnationis dominice millesimo ducentesimo octuagesimo sexto.
entries.english:
XL. Count Rudolf von Wertheim consents to Petrissa, widow of the knight Crafto von Reicholzheim, selling her properties there to Brombach Monastery. 1286.

In the name of the Lord, amen. We, Rudolf, Count von Wertheim, declare through these presents to all to whom this letter may come that Petrissa, widow of Crafto von Reicholzheim, and her daughter Agnes have sold to the brothers of Brombach Monastery, for fifty pounds in Heller received from them in ready money and put to their own use, all their properties at Reicholzheim. These include houses, pastures, meadows, waters, forests, cultivated and uncultivated fields, rents, and every other revenue which they possessed there by hereditary ownership or held from us as fiefs. They sold these properties to be held forever as absolute property. Herold, son of Otto von Heigenstat and son-in-law of the aforesaid Petrissa, consented to this transaction, with our assent and favor. Accordingly, whatever of the aforesaid properties Petrissa and her daughter Agnes appeared to hold as fiefs from us, they freely and unconditionally surrendered to us through the hands of Conrad von Klinghart, for Herold, Petrissa’s son-in-law, and all his heirs, giving their full consent in every respect to this transaction and to the terms set out above.

In view of the goodwill and devotion which the aforesaid brothers of Brombach have shown us, we freely and absolutely grant and give to them all the aforesaid properties to which we were entitled by reason of feudal right and our power to grant them, as true and free property in hope of and for the sake of eternal life, so that they may possess them forever with the full liberty and lawful rights of absolute ownership, notwithstanding any objection. In witness and proof of this, and so that no opportunity for doubt or dispute may arise later concerning these matters, we have caused this letter to be written and sealed with our seal and that of the venerable Abbot of Brombach, in whose presence all these matters were transacted. The witnesses are: Godfridus, nobleman of Schlüsselberg; Conrad Clinckart; Wolframus von Kuntech; Godfridus von Arrstein; Otto, son of Lupold; Cnappo, schultheiss zu Wertheim; Hermann Cellarius of the same place; Godfridus, his brother; Friedrich Nusekel; and many others. Done and given in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1286.
